newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening mixed to modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening mixed to modestly lower.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open mixed to slightly lower on Tuesday, extending some of Monday's choppiness and hampered by initial turbulence in the technology sector, analysts said.

Certain segments of the technology sector could experience selling pressure at the start after Seagate Technologies Inc, one of the country's largest makers of computer disk drives, warned its earnings for the latest quarter would be below expectations due to weak demand.

"Both Seagate and Cabletron said their quarters would fall short of expectations, which will put the technology sector under pressure," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said.

Cabletron Systems Inc said it expected first quarter earnings of about $0.37 per share, below analysts' estimates. It said demand appeared strong for its newer, high-end switching products and its Spectrum software, but softer for some of its other products.
"The Seagate news will drag down the disk makers and possibly the semiconductor stocks," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
Brown forecast a mixed opening with a possible rally to the upside later in the day, but said: "We need to get the technology sector back in gear before we see significant strength in the market."

The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was trading off 1.55 points at 844.65, while the long bond was up 4/32 at a 6.89 percent yield. Analysts said any decline in bond prices could send the stock market lower.

The main piece of the economic data for the bond market to digest on Tuesday is expected to be April leading indicators, due out at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. They were forecast to be unchanged versus a previous 0.1 percent rise.
Smaller-capitalization stocks, which fared better than blue chips on Monday, could do better than the Dow industrials again because listed stocks were overbought, one analyst said.
The Dow industrial average finished off 41.64 points at 7289.40 while the Nasdaq composite rose 4.47 to 1404.79. The Russell 2000 closed up 2.76 at 383.52.
Japan's Nikkei-225 index finished up 111.31 points at 20563.16.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 20.9 points at 4541.9. U.S. stocks were steady but volume was light.
The dollar weakened against the yen by late Tokyo, trading at 116.20/30 yen. In Europe, the dollar was trading at 1.7240/50 marks.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reported that many asset allocators were now cautious on the stock market and instead had shifted funds into bonds.

The New York Times reported in its Marketplace column that with Wall Street in the midst of a consolidation phase, many wonder what Lehman Brothers Holdings will do. Lehman Chairman Richard Fuld has said the firm is not looking to be bought but outsiders are not so sure.
